content: Copyleft is a concept that allows programs, software, literature, or other creative works to be freely modified by others. However, this freedom does not extend to reproducing, adapting, or distributing these works for commercial purposes. To identify copyleft sources, you should first check whether the work is produced by organizations other than the United States Federal Government, as such works may be protected by U.S. and international copyright laws. Look for the absence of a copyright symbol, the name of a copyright holder, or the statement All Rights Reserved. Instead, confirm the presence of licenses such as Creative Commons, ShareAlike, or GNU Free Documentation at the bottom of the page. The following is a list of resources that may contain copyleft information or media. It is important to note that not all content on these websites is necessarily copyleft. If you are uncertain, consult your deputy editor-in-chief for guidance. Medical Images The National Library of Medicine provides resources such as MedPix and Open-i, which may contain medical images under copyleft licenses. Websites The National Library of Medicine’s MedlinePlus The National Cancer Institute’s Physician Data Query (PDQ®) Libre Pathology Radiopaedia.org The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) SurgWiki The Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) program Ganfyd (Get A Note From Your Doctor) The National Eye Institute The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases The National Human Genome Research Institute The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute The National Institute of Mental Health The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke WikiBooks The ECG Learning Center All material from these websites should be properly referenced, including a link to the source page. Journals and Search Engines PLOS.org BioMed Central Springer Open Wiley Creative Commons Search Medical Wikis in English The following is a list of medical wikis in English.
